review_text: After posting this complaint, I was eventually contacted and reimbursed for the incompatible parts. However, after a few messages, the employee who had initially reached out to me appeared to stop responding, which forced me to contact the in-app support again. Only then was a warranty claim filed and my money refunded. While I am grateful for the resolution, I remain concerned about the way it was handled. The company referred to this outcome as a ‘gesture of goodwill.’ In reality, complying with consumer protection law is not goodwill—it is a legal obligation. What troubles me most is that, instead of straightforward assistance, I personally had to spend a great deal of time researching laws, studying specific legal articles, and presenting them to prove that I had the right to a refund. I appreciate the final resolution, but the process was unnecessarily time-consuming, frustrating, and placed the entire burden on me as the customer. Order number: 119912765 Order date: 10.09.2024 I am extremely disappointed with Autodoc’s customer service and their refusal to take responsibility for an incorrect part selection. All my previous orders for my Honda Accord 8 (VIN: JHMCU35809C203590) were always placed through Autodoc’s support team, never by myself. I always relied on their staff to provide the correct parts. However, in this case Autodoc now falsely claims that I ordered the parts on my own without their involvement, which is absolutely not true. The lower control arms that I received do not fit my vehicle. This is a clear case of “Sachmangel” under §434 BGB (German Civil Code) — the goods do not conform to the contract, as they are not suitable for the intended purpose. According to §439 BGB, in such cases the seller is obliged to provide a correct replacement or a full refund, and also to compensate the customer for costs of removal/installation. Instead, Autodoc is trying to hide behind a 14-day return period, which is irrelevant here. The 14-day return policy only applies to voluntary returns. When the goods are not as described or do not match the contract due to the seller’s mistake, the time limit does not apply — this is confirmed by EU consumer law (Directive 1999/44/EC and Directive (EU) 2019/771 on consumer sales and guarantees). In other words: •	The parts were selected incorrectly by Autodoc staff (as in all my previous orders). •	The parts do not fit — this is legally a non-conforming good. •	Autodoc must provide a replacement or refund under BGB §§434–439 and EU Directive 2019/771. •	Refusing support and shifting blame onto the customer is a breach of EU consumer rights. I am now forced to escalate this case to the European Consumer Centre (ECC-Net) and file a formal complaint. This whole experience has shown me that Autodoc’s customer support is unwilling to take responsibility when their own mistake causes problems for the buyer. ⚠️ Buyers beware: if Autodoc makes a mistake in selecting your parts, they will try to deny responsibility and hide behind irrelevant “return policies.”

review_text: This review is for the company Autodoc or autoteiledirekt.de (they seem to operate under a bunch of different names, so I posted here and on Autodoc reviews). The short version: Absolutely terrible customer service, bordering on a scam. Order somewhere else! The very long one for those who care: I ordered a bunch of parts from them and to be fair the items are what I expected and do their jobs but 2 days after the items were supposed to be at my house (shipped inside Germany so no excuse there) I called them up and after pretty unfriendly interaction with their customer service guy I got promised that it would go out that day. So, if it says 2 days, expect a week. While I was talking to him I noticed the parts where now 30 Euros cheaper on a 200 Euro order and I asked him for a deal. I would have taken store credit, even a complimentary sponge or a packet of gummy bears or something that showed any interest in their customers, but he wasn't willing to budge. Fair enough there too, they don't have to. So, I told him I would just order the stuff again and return the first package and since they already delivered the parts too late for me I had all the time in the world (second package was late by the same time frame too). I even bought their safe order (sicher bestellen) feature on the first order, which states that I can return the uninstalled parts for a full refund for any reason within a 100 days or something like that. Since the boxes are just sitting here and haven’t even been opened it shouldn't have been a problem. A week after I filed for the return I haven't even gotten a mail saying that it is being processed other than their automated instant reply so I called them up again. I didn’t even get an answer the first 4 times I called even though it kept telling me constantly I was next in line. After 15 Minutes and 27 Seconds you get dropped from the line each time so you get to try again. I have a headset and plenty of time while i was doing other things so I just kept calling. Even tried calling them from 3 lines at once (I got bored) and you get the same message on all of them. That was around 10am on a regular business day. Never got through to anyone then so I tried again in the afternoon and after the second round of waiting I actually got someone who couldn't even say hello or good bye or anything and I tried my best to be extra friendly. I got some results in the form of six emails (one for each part I ordered) saying my return was accepted and an attached PDF Return Form for every part. Seemed like progress but it also said that my return mailers would come in separate emails which still haven't arrived 5 days later. I guess I will listening to some more annoying music and automated messages next week. At this point I fully expect them to either not answer at all or at best be extremely rude again. Chances of me getting the full refund, that their extra safe order service promises are slim to none and I bet they will give me the full runaround for that too. Calling it what it is at this point is a Scam. I will change this review accordingly if they manage to surprise me and not do any of that, after all terrible service and late deliveries aren't a scam if the parts are what you bought but at this point it sure looks like a Scam when it comes to their return policies and safe order options. Update (26.06.2018): I guess complaining loudly on the internet does help since their english speaking customer service called me up first thing monday and sent me the return mailer (just one though even though I got two boxes but since they already had all the heavy stuff in one box and the 2 super light things in a seperate one I figured they might as well go in a single box. Didn't want to argue over this but I took a bunch of pictures anyway). The english speaking customer service rep was very nice, which was a welcome change so I guess I'll be carefully optimistic and wait. Update (09.07.2018): Turns out they actually did send me three labels - in yet again three separate emails - just two ended up in spam. I guess since it took 40something emails (not even kidding) to get to this point. So I sent the three packages in the same arrangement they came here and apparently they received them on Jul. 2nd. Still waiting to hear anything further. Don't hold your breath on getting your money in any sort of timely fashion back. Mind you I started the Process over a month ago on June 3rd. I do realize the return proves and banks and all that take their sweet time too. I don't have a problem with that, but this is just ridiculous. How does a company with that terrible of a customer service stay in business these days? I've head better customer service from Indian tech support scammers than these guys. review_text: Well, I wasn't sure about chip tuning… like… I really wasn’t sure. I had just bought my dream car – one that wasn’t killing the environment, but also had a bit of poke and gets me up and down the mountain that I live up in Austria – even in snow and ice.  (It’s a UK registered Jaguar XF 20 AWD with 180 ps and 430 nm). So, its a proper nice car, but not that pokey (acceleration) as I had been driving a Skoda VRS before, and that goes as fast as Donald J Trump after a cheeseburger, so, naturally after a while I began to think I really should have got the Jaguar 25 AWD with 241ps). It was then that I understood that essentially the two cars are identical (suspension, brakes, interior, etc.) with the exception that the ‘more powerful’ and much more expensive 25 AWD is just faster because of the twin turbo, so. Suddenly, I worked out, I might be able to get 25 AWD performance for a few hundred Euros, rather than several thousand it would get to buy the 25 AWD which are about 20% more expensive on the second hand market. So, I asked a mate of mine who drives ridiculous German cars: S6, AMG Jeep type thing – utterly bonkers. He doesn’t talk much normally (he just likes his cars), and his reaction was weird. For the first time in a lifetime he just wouldn’t shut up about how ‘effing brilliant chip tuning was. Well, that avalanche of praise from an otherwise ‘quiet man’ convinced me and the next day, I took the plunge and ordered the smallest chip (the S) to test it out and see what it might do. It arrived a couple of days later. The wife was curious (she always gets to the post first) and I told her it was a thing to save fuel. She was totally suspicious “Why doesn’t everyone have one then?” she asked. “Round here?” I countered looking up and down the valley. We live surrounded by mountain farmers who drive tractors by day and big Audis by night. “I expect most already do… Its only 169 Euros” I said. “I’ll order one for you tomorrow, just give me the cash.” I could see her weighing up how much cat food she could buy for that much money, and to be honest, it wasn’t even a mildly fair contest. Within seconds she was back to annimal videos on her phone.  Job done. With that now taken care of, it was time to get it installed. Well, I’m an academic by trade, so more of a philospohy type, than a spanner and wrench one; not really very ‘hands on’, but also not stupid. Anyway, it took me about 10 minutes to get it all wired up, they give you a whole bunch of instructions (with pictures), that make IKEA building look difficult, so its really a nice piece of customer service. With this done, I then took the Jag out for a test drive, and the difference was noticeable. I had been missing that little kick in the small of the back when accelerating (yes, sad but true, I have been missing the little VRS – who would believe it?), and now, it seemed like the Jag had suddenly gone from a nice looker, to a ‘nearly’ exciting performer.  I drove up and down the mountain once on the winding serpentine roads; night time, all to myself, and sure enough, found myself grinning like a school boy. There you go compatriots, that is what you need. That is the real test, whether it makes you smile or not, and it did… but, not quite enough. I realised I needed the bigger chip, the GTS. (Naturally, there is a whole marketing strategy behind the chip tuning industry, and I am now in the thick of it). Well, there you go, that’s my story. In my opinion, the thing to look out for (especially in a diesel like my Jag XF and it’ll be the same in a 5 series or an A6, or an E class) is how much the torque increases - not so much the Horse Power.: although to be fair, they say the ps has gone from 180 to 214 PS, so that's not bad either What you are looking at is a signficant power gain further down the rev spectrum, say mid- 2k for nm: as well as a noticiable one than over 5k for bp. So, this means when your mates down the pub (Kneipe for my German friends; Wirtshaus where I live), ask you (as they will) 'Wieviel PS alter?", and with the GTS chip (the big brother) you have to talk about the stonking, beautiful, galvansing 540 nm you have (and possibly leave out the 230 ps). Thing is, you don't get to honestly say “380 ps alter”, which is what the big V6 3.0 Diesel Jaguar has with EXACTLY THE SAME amount of Newtons as the GTS chip would give my modest cat!!! At the moment my RaceChip ‘S’ tuned Jag has 503 NM with a chip that cost me 160 Euros, and if I do eventually decide to get the GTS chip, and drive around with 540 Newtownians, I may not have the nervy-edgy racy feel of 380 horses, but I will have the firm, powerful push with more NM than the brand new ‘BMW 540’, with only 500 nm. I will have 5 more nm than the legendary 2020 Porsche Carrera 4S, for considerably less, and that is probably ‘it’ in a nutshell. "More for less". There, put that in your pipe and smoke it.

review_text: Absolutely avoid this product!! I'd like to address a few issues with this product which have also been highlighted by others. I Bought the GTS model, upon arrival it came with generic instructions, whilst I appreciate those who are absolute car enthusiast may know where to find the turbo pressure sensor and Map sensor, for the average person just wanting to do a little extra to there car this isnt as straight forward. You have to email them to obtain instructions specifically for your vehicle and from reading their FAQ this is clearly a problem that many consumers have had and never actually been addressed. When you're paying £300 + for a product I'd expect some instructions. After joining other Facebook forums I managed to obtain instructions from other sources as racechip took so long to reply I managed to get it fitted. Upon initially driving the car you can notice the difference almost immediately, clear power and torque increase and loved it. All to good to be true after about a week I began to notice my rev counter appeared to be slipping whilst the chip was on and happened regardless of what mode it was in (race, sport, eco). Approximately 1 week after this my car began judder and was hesitant when putting my foot down and again revs kept slipping. I made contact with racechip and they advised that they would send a new update to my chip, this process was quick to install but the problems I've mentioned above became even more apparent. This Monday I decided I want to nip to shop and get some stuff, not long after I left the house I noticed the issues again and began to smell oil coming through my air vents and smoke from the engine bay. When I stopped and lifted the bonnet it looked like there had been and explosion of oil, immediately began to think I blew a head gasket or done some damage to the engine. Later took it into the garage and it turned out to just be a cylinder head cap and seal that had come off and shot oil all over the side of the engine. I didn't initially think it was anything to do with the racechip and but it down to just wear and tear of the engine and my luck really. Managed to get this replaced and decided to turn off the chip for a while because of the hot weather and possibly causing any more damage to the engine. Since doing that the car ran really smooth again and had absolutely know issues up until I decided to turn the chip back on today and put it into eco mode. I took about a 10 min drive to my local asda and on the way back began to notice similar issues that I mentioned at the start again, about 500m from my house loss power again and smell of oil began to fill the air vents again. Due to what previously happened I decided to check the same area where the original repairs were made and immediately noticed the 2nd cylinder head cap and seal had come off and shot oil all over the engine again. Tomorrow I intend on completely removing the chip from my car and returning it back to how it was, I can't obviously say that the issues I've had have all been down to the chip but this is the only variable I have changed on the car and only noticed them whilst the chip is active. It appears that there is just too much pressure and stress being put on the engine and Im gonna try and prevent anything further happening to my car. I wish I had listened to the other reviews people had said about tuning chips and in particularly racechip but I gave them the benefit of the doubt and became a foolish consumer of the product. This is my warning to all those out there who want to make changes to your car, do not buy this product, get your car remapped professionally if you intend to do anything. From reading other recent reviews I have seen that people just end up getting into a back and forth war with racechip about the faults with this product and there reluctance to help. With that I am just going to learn my lesson, cut my losses and never purchase another tuning chip.

review_text: This review is for the company Autodoc or autoteiledirekt.de (they seem to operate under a bunch of different names, so I posted here and on Autodoc reviews).The short version: Absolutely terrible customer service, bordering on a scam. Order somewhere else!The very long one for those who care:I ordered a bunch of parts from them and to be fair the items are what I expected and do their jobs but 2 days after the items were supposed to be at my house (shipped inside Germany so no excuse there) I called them up and after pretty unfriendly interaction with their customer service guy I got promised that it would go out that day. So, if it says 2 days, expect a week.While I was talking to him I noticed the parts where now 30 Euros cheaper on a 200 Euro order and I asked him for a deal. I would have taken store credit, even a complimentary sponge or a packet of gummy bears or something that showed any interest in their customers, but he wasn't willing to budge. Fair enough there too, they don't have to.So, I told him I would just order the stuff again and return the first package and since they already delivered the parts too late for me I had all the time in the world (second package was late by the same time frame too). I even bought their safe order (sicher bestellen) feature on the first order, which states that I can return the uninstalled parts for a full refund for any reason within a 100 days or something like that. Since the boxes are just sitting here and haven’t even been opened it shouldn't have been a problem.A week after I filed for the return I haven't even gotten a mail saying that it is being processed other than their automated instant reply so I called them up again. I didn’t even get an answer the first 4 times I called even though it kept telling me constantly I was next in line. After 15 Minutes and 27 Seconds you get dropped from the line each time so you get to try again. I have a headset and plenty of time while i was doing other things so I just kept calling. Even tried calling them from 3 lines at once (I got bored) and you get the same message on all of them. That was around 10am on a regular business day. Never got through to anyone then so I tried again in the afternoon and after the second round of waiting I actually got someone who couldn't even say hello or good bye or anything and I tried my best to be extra friendly. I got some results in the form of six emails (one for each part I ordered) saying my return was accepted and an attached PDF Return Form for every part. Seemed like progress but it also said that my return mailers would come in separate emails which still haven't arrived 5 days later.I guess I will listening to some more annoying music and automated messages next week. At this point I fully expect them to either not answer at all or at best be extremely rude again. Chances of me getting the full refund, that their extra safe order service promises are slim to none and I bet they will give me the full runaround for that too.Calling it what it is at this point is a Scam.I will change this review accordingly if they manage to surprise me and not do any of that, after all terrible service and late deliveries aren't a scam if the parts are what you bought but at this point it sure looks like a Scam when it comes to their return policies and safe order options.Update (26.06.2018):I guess complaining loudly on the internet does help since their english speaking customer service called me up first thing monday and sent me the return mailer (just one though even though I got two boxes but since they already had all the heavy stuff in one box and the 2 super light things in a seperate one I figured they might as well go in a single box. Didn't want to argue over this but I took a bunch of pictures anyway). The english speaking customer service rep was very nice, which was a welcome change so I guess I'll be carefully optimistic and wait.Update (09.07.2018):Turns out they actually did send me three labels - in yet again three separate emails - just two ended up in spam. I guess since it took 40something emails (not even kidding) to get to this point. So I sent the three packages in the same arrangement they came here and apparently they received them on Jul. 2nd. Still waiting to hear anything further. Don't hold your breath on getting your money in any sort of timely fashion back. Mind you I started the Process over a month ago on June 3rd. I do realize the return proves and banks and all that take their sweet time too. I don't have a problem with that, but this is just ridiculous. How does a company with that terrible of a customer service stay in business these days? I've head better customer service from Indian tech support scammers than these guys. I’m curious what happens next. My guess is I do get some money back at some point or another but not even close to the amount I paid with all kinds of bogus charges and “service” fees as a justification. I guess we will see.
